description: A class implementing `IHostedService` that the host starts with the app and stops on graceful shutdown, registered with `AddHostedService` as a singleton.
The base class for long-running hosted services: you override `ExecuteAsync`, whose returned task is the lifetime of the service.
The cancellation token passed to `ExecuteAsync`, cancelled when the host stops, which every loop and async call in the service should observe.
Creating a DI scope with `IServiceScopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope()` for each tick, message or job, so scoped services such as `DbContext` live only as long as that work.
An async timer whose `WaitForNextTickAsync` drives interval loops without overlapping iterations.
The host option that decides what an unhandled exception in `ExecuteAsync` does; the default since .NET 6, `StopHost`, logs it and stops the host.
The `dotnet new worker` template: a host built with `Host.CreateApplicationBuilder` and the `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Worker` SDK, with DI, configuration and logging but no HTTP server.
